reuse.why: Uses existing setBudget/batchMessages/isTrackingBudget/getSheetValue, but never introduces or reuses a single category-selection definition; each action keeps its own query.

duplication.why: The same eligibility SQL (hidden toggle, #fixed group notes, goal_def IS NULL) is pasted into setZero, setLastMonthSpending, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg and set12MonthAvg, and re-expressed a sixth time as JS ifs in copyPreviousMonth.

placement.why: All logic stays in budget/actions.ts with the handler registered in app.ts, matching where the tree keeps month-wide actions.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the bulk actions, the new handler and tests for the requested behaviour.

maintainability.why: Each new exclusion rule had to be edited in six places, and the next rule will too; the copies already differ in form (SQL vs JS) and can drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No shared category-selection helper existed in actions.ts before the change; the diff neither has one to bypass nor creates one.

disguised_duplication.where: copyPreviousMonth re-expresses the same eligibility rule as JS conditions on getBudgetData rows (group_notes/goal_def/hidden) instead of the SQL WHERE used by the other five actions.

abstraction_drift.where: No shared selection helper; across the four steps the exclusion rule (templates, hidden, #fixed, includeHiddenCategories) is re-implemented at all six month-wide actions in actions.ts (copyPreviousMonth, setZero, setLastMonthSpending, set3/6/12MonthAvg).
